clips.send: Pins (键 jiàn). Bronze pins the parts turn on. Two pins go right through the housing and the stock.
clips.text: Pins (键 jiàn)。Bronze pins the parts turn on。Two pins go right through the housing and the stock.

clips.send: Crossbow square (kneeling and standing). The front corner of Pit 2. Kneeling crossbowmen in the middle, standing archers around them. One idea: one group shoots while the other reloads, so the arrows never stop. An L-shaped pit with four mixed units; roughly 1,300 figures and 80+ chariots (approximate).
clips.text: Crossbow square (kneeling and standing)。The front corner of Pit 2。Kneeling crossbowmen in the middle, standing archers around them.。One idea: one group shoots while the other reloads, so the arrows never stop.。An L-shaped pit with four mixed units; roughly 1,300 figures and 80+ chariots (approximate).

clips.send: Armoured infantry. Filling the long corridors of Pit 1. The main body of the army: thousands of soldiers in armour, in columns four wide. They carried long bronze weapons such as spears and halberds (戈, 矛, 戟). About 230 m times 62 m (755 times 203 ft) — longer than two US football fields. Estimated ~6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

Estimated ~6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

clips.send: Shaanxi.
clips.text: Shaanxi.

clips.send: Teeth (牙 yá). Two bronze hooks that catch and hold the string. When you cock the crossbow, the string is pulled back and locks behind the teeth. The teeth and the sight are one piece that turns on a bronze pin.

clips.send: Tianjin.
clips.text: Tianjin.

clips.send: Gansu.
clips.text: Gansu.

clips.send: Vanguard: archers and crossbowmen. The 3 front rows at the east end of Pit 1. About 200 figures in 3 rows face the enemy first. Most wear battle robes but no armour — light and quick. Their job: shoot first, from long range. About 230 m times 62 m (755 times 203 ft) — longer than two US football fields. Estimated ~6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

clips.send: Beijing.
clips.text: Beijing.

clips.send: String (弦 xián). Pushes the bolt forward when released. A complete Qin crossbow found in the pits still had traces of a string thought to be made of animal tendon.
clips.text: String (弦 xián)。Pushes the bolt forward when released。A complete Qin crossbow found in the pits still had traces of a string thought to be made of animal tendon.

clips.send: Stock (臂 bì). The wooden body with a groove for the bolt. The wood has rotted away in the pits; the bronze parts survived.
clips.text: Stock (臂 bì)。The wooden body with a groove for the bolt。The wood has rotted away in the pits; the bronze parts survived.

clips.send: Trigger (悬刀 xuándāo). The hanging “knife” you pull to shoot. A small pull on a long lever releases a huge force: that is leverage.
clips.text: Trigger (悬刀 xuándāo)。The hanging “knife” you pull to shoot。A small pull on a long lever releases a huge force: that is leverage.

clips.send: Shanxi.
clips.text: Shanxi.

clips.send: Bolt (矢 shǐ). A short arrow with a bronze three-sided head. Tens of thousands of bronze arrowheads have been found with the Terracotta Army.
clips.text: Bolt (矢 shǐ)。A short arrow with a bronze three-sided head。Tens of thousands of bronze arrowheads have been found with the Terracotta Army.

clips.send: Command post. Pit 3, the smallest pit. Only 68 figures: guards lining the walls, facing each other, and one chariot. It is thought to be the headquarters that commanded the army in Pits 1 and 2. A small U-shaped pit with 68 figures and one chariot: the command post.
clips.text: Command post。Pit 3, the smallest pit。Only 68 figures: guards lining the walls, facing each other, and one chariot.。It is thought to be the headquarters that commanded the army in Pits 1 and 2.。A small U-shaped pit with 68 figures and one chariot: the command post.

clips.send: Sight (望山 wàngshān). The aiming blade — like the sight on a rifle. It sticks up when the crossbow is cocked. Line it up with the target. Some Han-dynasty sights even had a scale of marks for different distances.
clips.text: Sight (望山 wàngshān)。The aiming blade — like the sight on a rifle。It sticks up when the crossbow is cocked. Line it up with the target.。Some Han-dynasty sights even had a scale of marks for different distances.

clips.send: Bow (弓 gōng). Stores energy when it bends. The harder the bow is to bend, the more energy it stores — and the faster the bolt flies.
clips.text: Bow (弓 gōng)。Stores energy when it bends。The harder the bow is to bend, the more energy it stores — and the faster the bolt flies.

clips.send: Xinjiang.
clips.text: Xinjiang.

clips.send: Housing (郭 guō). The bronze box that holds all the parts together. Archaeologists found Qin trigger parts made to very similar sizes — almost like standard spare parts.

clips.send: Ningxia.
clips.text: Ningxia.

clips.send: Rear guard. The last rows at the west end, facing backwards. They guard the army’s back. About 230 m times 62 m (755 times 203 ft) — longer than two US football fields. Estimated ~6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

clips.send: Liaoning.
clips.text: Liaoning.

clips.send: Flank guards. The outer rows along the north and south sides. The outermost soldiers face outwards, so the army can’t be attacked from the side. About 230 m times 62 m (755 times 203 ft) — longer than two US football fields. Estimated ~6,000 clay soldiers and horses.

clips.text: Inner Mongolia.

clips.send: Battle of Muye. c. 1046 BC. Muye, near today’s Xinxiang, Henan Province. Zhou + allied tribes (King Wu) vs Shang (King Zhou 纣王). Zhou wins. The Shang dynasty falls and the Western Zhou begins, with its capital at Haojing. 不战而屈人之兵, 善之善者也. The very best victory makes the enemy give up without a fight.

clips.send: 侧翼。南北两侧最外面的队列。最外侧的士兵面朝外，防止敌人从侧面进攻。。东西长约230米、南北宽约62米，比两个美式橄榄球场还长。估计有约6000件陶俑、陶马。

clips.send: 弓弦。松开时把箭推出去。俑坑中发现的一件完整秦弩上，残留着据认为用动物筋腱制成的弓弦痕迹。

clips.send: 牧野之战。约公元前1046年。牧野（今河南新乡一带）。周武王及各部落联军 对 商纣王。周胜。商朝灭亡，西周建立，定都镐京。。不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也。。不经过交战就使敌人屈服，才是高明中最高明的。

clips.send: 铠甲步兵俑。排满一号坑的各条过洞。军阵的主体：成千上万身披铠甲的步兵，四路纵队排列。。手持戈、矛、戟等长兵器。。东西长约230米、南北宽约62米，比两个美式橄榄球场还长。估计有约6000件陶俑、陶马。

clips.send: 弩箭（矢）。带三棱形青铜箭头的短箭。兵马俑坑出土了数以万计的青铜箭头。
clips.text: 弩箭（矢）。带三棱形青铜箭头的短箭。兵马俑坑出土了数以万计的青铜箭头。

clips.send: 牙。钩住弓弦的两个铜钩。上弦时把弦拉到后面，扣在牙上。。牙和望山连成一体，绕着铜键转动。
clips.text: 牙。钩住弓弦的两个铜钩。上弦时把弦拉到后面，扣在牙上。。牙和望山连成一体，绕着铜键转动。

clips.send: 望山。瞄准用的部件，像步枪上的准星和标尺。上弦后它会竖起来，用它对准目标。。有些汉代弩机的望山上还刻有刻度，用来估计距离。

clips.send: 郭。把各个零件装在一起的青铜外匣。考古学家发现，秦代弩机零件的尺寸非常统一，几乎可以互换。

clips.send: 前锋：弓弩手。一号坑东端最前面的三排。约200个陶俑排成三排，最先面对敌人。。他们大多身穿战袍，不披铠甲，行动轻快。。任务：远距离率先射击。。东西长约230米、南北宽约62米，比两个美式橄榄球场还长。估计有约6000件陶俑、陶马。

clips.send: 弩弓。弯曲时储存能量。弓越难拉开，储存的能量越多，箭飞得越快。

clips.send: 后卫。西端最后几排，面朝后方。保护军阵的后方。。东西长约230米、南北宽约62米，比两个美式橄榄球场还长。估计有约6000件陶俑、陶马。

clips.send: 弩臂。木制的弩身，上面有放箭的槽。俑坑里的木质部分已经腐朽，青铜零件保存了下来。

clips.send: 悬刀。扣动它就能发射，因形状像挂着的刀而得名。在长杠杆上轻轻一扣，就能释放巨大的力量——这就是杠杆原理。
